empires.name: The Norse Jarldoms
empires.note: The sea is their road, not their edge. Longships draw a foot of water - they beach on any coast, row up any river, and are gone before your levy has formed.

places.name: Uppsala
places.note: The throne. Nine days of sacrifice at the great temple, and every jarl in the north arrives armed.

places.name: Hedeby
places.note: Wedged between two seas behind an earth rampart; silver from half the world changes hands here.

places.name: Birka
places.note: An island market on the lake - furs, slaves, foreign coin, and a garrison hall smaller than the warehouses.

places.name: Nidaros
places.note: A day of rowing up the fjord to reach it; take the shallows wrong and you sit on mud until the tide.

places.name: Kaupang
places.note: A summer market and nothing else - come in winter and you burn empty sheds.

places.name: Ribe
places.note: Tidal marsh on every approach; ships come up the creek at high water or wait a day.

places.name: Lund
places.note: Flat plain all around - they watch you walk inland from the beach for half a morning.

places.name: Bjorgvin
places.note: Rain most days, mountains at its back, and dried cod stacked in every shed.

places.name: Reykjavik
places.note: Steam off the hot springs, no wall and no lord - the farms lie a day apart.

empires.name: The Aztec Empire
empires.note: Across the western ocean, off the edge of every chart you own. They fight the flower wars and take men alive - lose here and you are walked up the temple steps, so a defeat is something you escape from rather than die in.

places.name: Tenochtitlan
places.note: The throne. An island city on a lake, three causeways in, and every one of them can be cut behind you.

places.name: Texcoco
places.note: The east shore - law courts, singers, and the dike that keeps the salt water off the capital.

places.name: Tlacopan
places.note: Least of the three thrones and it knows it; the western causeway starts at its gate.

places.name: Cholollan
places.note: A pilgrim town under the largest pyramid standing - more priests than warriors, and tribute piled in every court.

places.name: Tlaxcallan
places.note: Ringed by the empire on all sides and never taken; they hate Tenochtitlan more than they will ever hate you.

places.name: Xochimilco
places.note: Garden plots floating in the shallows - the city's larder, defended by mud and canals.

places.name: Huaxyacac
places.note: A garrison planted far down the southern road, holding a valley that resents it.

places.name: Tepeyacac
places.note: Every carrier train bound for the coast halts here; the market runs whether there is a war or not.

places.name: Malinalco
places.note: A temple cut into the cliff above the houses, and the path up takes men one at a time.
